_comment: Battle AI phase 1 (#584) showcase: three unit-leader decisions issued as real queue orders, with no direct target_enemy write. (1) The AI spearmen (anti_cavalry) on the left forms the anti-cavalry square on its own as player cavalry closes -- no player key press arms it, unlike the player-driven anti-cav-square.json demo. (2) The AI infantry on the right advances and attacks the player infantry it's assigned (the advance/attack fallback, now a real ATTACK order) while a second player unit is walked onto its flank; the AI leader reacts by re-facing onto the flanker. Deterministic (scenario + seed + scripted input).

overlap.reason: uid 1 (team 1's 140-strong spearmen block) is mid-transit through a SECOND forced re-slot for the whole catalog-cadence sampling window. The AI's ATTACK order re-targets from enemy uid 0 to uid 2 around tick ~302-310 (target_enemy_uid flips, facing swings from ~[0.97,-0.08] toward [-0.55,0.83] and back), and that order re-stamp calls Unit.start_order_response() -> reform_ranks(), which re-arms the standoff settle window (Unit._standoff_settle_until_tick, read by SoldierBodies, #1537) and re-slots the entire block onto a freshly-rotated grid before the FIRST reform (from the tick~150 in-place REFORM phase while the order was still MOVE; the MOVE->ATTACK order change itself lands between ticks 240 and 250) has even finished converging (own_slot_dist_med was down to ~7.9 wu at tick 300, then jumps back to ~78.5 wu at tick 310). A 140-body block takes several hundred ticks to walk back onto a fully-rotated grid, and while it does, files legitimately cross each other, so SoldierBodies' nearest-neighbour distance dips under the foot floor mid-crossing (measured worst 1.755 wu against the 2.25 wu floor at ~tick 420, on current main after #1538's derate) even though the standoff pass is doing its job of policing that crossing, not causing it. Measured 2026-09-08 at the website catalog cadence (issue #1544).

shape_residual.reason: Same re-slot-before-settling mechanism as the overlap exemption above: uid 1's grid is still walking onto its second, freshly-rotated set of target slots at every catalog-cadence sample tick from ~310 through the end of the clip, so the best-fit rigid-transform residual against the (already-superseded) prior orientation stays large the whole time (measured worst 29.26 wu against the 6.75 wu threshold, at ~tick 420). It is genuinely converging (own_slot_dist_med falls from ~78.5 wu at tick 310 to ~0.38 wu by tick 720), just too slowly for a 140-man block to settle within this clip's length once the AI's mid-march re-target restarted the reform. Measured 2026-09-08 (issue #1544).

path_crossing.reason: Direct consequence of the same forced re-slot: rotating a 140-body grid ~90+ degrees mid-march genuinely sends a real fraction of the block's files along crossing routes to their new slots, which is exactly what the path_crossing metric is designed to flag on a bad ROUTE even when the end state looks fine. Measured worst 0.479 against the 0.15 threshold. Not a routing bug distinct from the overlap/shape_residual findings above -- same mechanism, same tick window. Measured 2026-09-08 (issue #1544).
